item.text:
**Decision.** Give dispatchers an online web console in managed Chrome and Safari to view schedules, assign jobs, and review synchronized inspections. Defer a native macOS client until a macOS-only need emerges. Keep technicians on Android for assigned jobs, inspections, photo capture, and up to 48 hours offline, with Room queuing submissions and WorkManager retrying sync. [`MIG-AW-OPS` §1] [`MIG-AW-APP` §§1–2] [`MIG-AW-BRIEF` §1]

**Data.** Copying Room is not a viable migration path. Its encryption key is device-bound, there is no documented export or restore flow, and queued inspections may be unsent. Read jobs and accepted inspections from the authoritative server. [`MIG-AW-APP` §2] [`MIG-AW-API` §§1–2]

**Proof of concept.** Use one test job and one photo. In each managed browser, verify sign-in, session handling, and CORS for API and upload requests. Time one schedule-to-assignment task against the current process. Force a stale `If-Match` update, confirm `409 Conflict`, then refresh and retry. Replay one inspection with the same `submissionId` and verify exactly one accepted record. Test browser file access and signed-URL renewal after 20 minutes, retaining the photo until acknowledgement. Verify the inspection is visible for review. Browser compatibility, including Safari upload behavior, remains unverified. [`MIG-AW-API` §§1–3] [`MIG-AW-OPS` §§1–2]

**Gate.** Pilot with two dispatchers. Expand only if both browsers pass every check, assignment time meets the measured baseline, and Android sync continues. Otherwise disable the console and resume prior dispatch operations. Estimate after the pilot. The six-week, 11-screen proposal is unverified. [`MIG-AW-OPS` §2] [`MIG-AW-BRIEF` §1]
